executiveSummary: GM1705's 2025 identity, Gelderland province and Gelderland-Midden safety-region assignment are coherent. The fresh full boundary contains the generated centre and CBS reports 47,684 residents; 42 neighbourhood rows sum to 47,665 (-19, -0.040%), consistent with annual rounding/suppression. Eight districts, eight BAG places and 22 BRT settlement labels are present. Ressen's BAG label point falls outside the independently versioned generalized polygon, while the simulation centre and full-boundary checks pass; that is a geometry-edition/generalization caveat, not evidence that Ressen is outside Lingewaard. All ten presets execute deterministically at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 across all eight services and pass numerical contracts. Release is nevertheless correction-required. Lingewaard lies between the Waal, Pannerdensch Kanaal and Nederrijn and depends on distinct primary-defence, outer-dike, seepage, Linge-inlet and urban/rural drainage mechanisms. The generic river preset selects none of them but holds normalized inundation stress 2.808170 through T+72, reaches 24,036 affected resident-equivalents and accumulates 1,685,871 person-hours. Seven unrelated individual hazards and the compound preset reuse a common neighbourhood order. Public observations show reduced Pannerdensch discharge/Nederrijn level and forecasts only through T+24; a water-board lifecycle record shows temporary Pannerling pumps used during extreme low water and removed once the fixed pump resumed, while water shortage remained. The 3 September reference window also contains a published Rijndijk closure between Angeren and Doornenburg, absent from the graph. A15 and N325/A325 logical records do not prove independent redundancy, live passage or access to cross-boundary emergency departments. Exact utilities, care, mobility, supply and first-72-hour recovery remain unsupported by operator topology, state, resources and completed actions. Unknown/NoData never means zero, safe, open or available.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — Full municipality geometry, settlement, road, rail and scheduled-transit reference inputs
evidenceSources.edition: 2025 boundary/statistics and generated BAG, BRT, NWB, ProRail and GTFS snapshots retrieved through 3 September 2026
supports: The generated centre [5.951571658981289, 51.905214160755676] is inside the fresh non-generalized 2025 municipality boundary.

The bundle contains eight districts, 42 neighbourhoods and the eight BAG places Angeren, Bemmel, Doornenburg, Gendt, Haalderen, Huissen, Loo Gld and Ressen. It also contains 22 BRT labels: seven woonkernen, four deelkernen, three gehuchten and eight buurtschappen.

Ressen's BAG label point falls outside the separately versioned generalized boundary. The full-boundary municipality and centre checks pass, so this is retained as a geometry-edition/generalization caveat rather than reassignment or exclusion.

Three logical road links expose A15 to Overbetuwe, N325 to Arnhem and A325 to Overbetuwe. N325/A325 are one numbered corridor family and are not additive independent resilience. No ProRail station is inside GM1705; GTFS supplies 80 scheduled stop areas.

CBS boundary OGC is CC BY 4.0; BAG is daily/Public Domain Mark 1.0; BRT is CC BY 4.0; NWB-Light is monthly/CC0; ProRail station geometry is CC0. GTFS is best-effort schedule context, not live service.

evidenceSources.title: E03 — Lingewaard Adaptatiestrategie and current climate-adaptation programme
evidenceSources.edition: Lingewaard Adaptatiestrategie 2021; implementation programme 2022–2026, current status page inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The municipality's stress test distinguishes paved-core cloudburst exposure, high groundwater and seepage behind dikes when river levels are high, soil/watercourse storage differences, low-groundwater/subsidence and restricted river-water intake under drought/low flow, and stronger heat in built-up areas.

The municipality describes itself as sensitive to very sensitive across climate effects and reports measures such as larger sewers, infiltration, water storage, an Angeren weir and studies with the water board. These are planning/implementation records, not current capacity or completed incident action.

A useful local input needs the native stress-test surface and scenario definition, CRS, resolution, rainfall/hydrograph, uncertainty, licence and NoData. The public PDF/site did not expose a blanket machine-reuse licence or live sewer/groundwater/pump state.
Static vulnerability and policy horizon remain distinct from observation, forecast, official incident scenario and synthetic model output.

evidenceSources.title: E04 — Primary defences along Waal, Pannerdensch Kanaal and Nederrijn and LIWO scenario requirements
evidenceSources.edition: Sterreschans–Huissen page published 15 April and updated 10 July 2026; LIWO release 2025.1.6
supports: The 9.2 km Sterreschans–Huissen reach lies in Lingewaard along the Pannerdensch Kanaal/Nederrijn. The water board states the dike is currently safe but parts do not meet future statutory requirements and describes height, stability, piping and wall concerns. Future strengthening is not present failure, and current safety is not an all-clear for an arbitrary breach event.

Sprok–Sterreschans–Heteren spans the Waal, Pannerdensch Kanaal and Nederrijn sides. Huissen–Elden is separately described as meeting the standard, so defence reaches and mechanisms must not be collapsed into one municipality scalar.

LIWO 2025.1.6 is professional scenario-selection context requiring expert interpretation. A usable case must retain source river, hydrograph/discharge, defence or breach, outer-dike/connected footprint, depth/velocity datum and units, arrival/duration/recession, edition, CRS/resolution, uncertainty, licence and NoData.
Project pages are public authority context with no blanket standard machine licence identified; LIWO scenario/model artefacts require their own catalogue and reuse metadata.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — Linge water-supply lifecycle, current drought updates and public water assets
evidenceSources.edition: Operational weblog through 3 September 2026; HWH snapshot retrieved 3 September 2026 01:38Z
supports: The Linge begins at Doornenburg and receives Pannerdensch Kanaal water through Pannerling. On 19 August the water board reported that exceptional Rhine/Waal low water had stopped the fixed Pannerling intake to prevent damage and that temporary lower-capacity pumps supplied the Linge.

Later operational updates supersede that state: increased river level allowed Pannerling to resume, both temporary Pannerling pumps were removed by the late-August update, and on 3 September the board still reported a water shortage while removing other temporary measures. Every state needs issue, valid-from/to and supersession semantics.

The current public asset screen assigns 103 points: eleven sewer pumps, eight surface-water pumps, RWZI Gendt and 83 weirs. Pannerling is registered as an intake pump with capacity 360, but native unit, connected topology, command, power/backup, staffing and live operation are not established by the aggregate.

HWH is partial/contributor-dependent official context retrieved 2026-09-03T01:38:15.250Z under CC BY-SA 4.0 and affectsSimulation=false. Registered status is not live operation; unknown topology/settings/state remain Unknown.

evidenceSources.publisher: Gemeente Lingewaard / Provincie Gelderland / Rijkswaterstaat / ProRail / OVapi
evidenceSources.title: E06 — Reference-window Rijndijk closure and regional transport dependencies
evidenceSources.edition: Municipal notice issued 11 August 2026, valid 24 August through 2 October 2026; NWB-Light 1 August 2026 and GTFS/ProRail snapshots through 3 September
supports: The municipality says Rijndijk between Scherpekamp in Angeren and Krakkedel in Doornenburg is closed from 24 August through 2 October for the ViA15 construction road. Traffic is diverted over Lodderhoeksestraat/N838, with extra morning congestion and school-day traffic control anticipated.

That restriction overlaps the audit's 3 September reference and the entire first 72 hours, but the public-context screen contains zero GM1705 NDW situations and the logical graph does not encode this local edge or detour. Empty NDW matching is NoData, not proof of open roads.

A15 and N325/A325 connect across municipality borders toward Overbetuwe/Arnhem, but three logical endpoints are not three independent corridors and their 260/150 scenario ceilings are not observed vehicles per hour or emergency capacity.

No ProRail station lies inside GM1705 and 80 GTFS stops are schedule geometry only. The Arnhem–Nijmegen–Foodvalley concession includes Lingewaard from 28 June 2026, but schedules and concession scope do not prove live vehicle, driver, accessibility, evacuation or restoration capacity.

NWB and ProRail carry CC0 source terms; the municipal notice has no blanket machine licence identified and must retain authority, publication and validity rather than be scraped into an unbounded permanent closure.

evidenceSources.edition: Current phase page inspected 3 September 2026; nature-season notice 16 April 2026

Staatsbosbeheer places Fort Pannerden at the Waal/Pannerdensch Kanaal split inside the rough-grazed Klompenwaard and describes Gendtsche and Bemmelse Waard within Gelderse Poort. This establishes local nature, recreation, access and smoke eligibility, not ignition, perimeter or occupants.

National 72-hour-kit guidance is a preparedness target, not observed household water, food, medicines, radio/power, mobility or support-network readiness. No blanket machine licence was identified for the dynamic phase or area pages.

Flood outcomes require river hydrographs, reach/defence state, outer-dike and breach/overtopping footprints, arrival, duration, recession and uncertainty; point observations and short forecasts are not inundation surfaces.
